Revert "feat(ai): publish window route state as a Mastra state signal (server half)"

This reverts commit d0ad65a13.

Parking the move to native state signals. The publish half works — lanes,
dedupe and ifIdle:'persist' were all verified live — but the signals never
reach the model, and the reason is structural rather than a missing tweak:
resolveStateSignalHistory is reachable only from "[Processor:<id>]
computeStateSignal". Mastra does not inject state signals into a prompt on its
own. Consuming them means writing an input processor that renders state into
the prompt — which is the job formatAgentUiStateHarnessInstructions already
does today, with four migrations of setup around it and nothing deleted in
exchange.

So this removes a POST /ai/v1/threads/:threadId/state that no client calls. An
unreachable write endpoint on the AI service is a surface to defend, not a
head start, and a dead code path rots faster than it would cost to retype.

Deliberately NOT reverted, because they are bugs on their own merits and were
only found through this work:
  18d275c80  ai.thread_message dropped ALL Mastra content.metadata
  85ec327d7  storage coerced role "signal" into "system"
The enum value and the metadata column stay: they make our storage a faithful
Mastra store, whether or not we ever send a state signal.

Still worth revisiting if Mastra starts injecting state signals natively, or
for a coordinator that must observe a user's navigation between turns — the one
property our per-run instruction block genuinely cannot provide.

Frontend tools (navigate, theme, etc.) suspended on every call and asked
the user to approve or reject before the browser handler ran, regardless
of what the tool actually did. Risk lives in what an action does, not in
dispatching a browser-side tool call — and this gate did not work
reliably. Guarding genuinely destructive actions belongs to connector
approval policies and prompts, not the tool boundary.

Frontend tools now always auto-execute: useAutoResolveFrontendTool (was
useAutoResolveSafeFrontendTool) resolves every frontend_tool interrupt
unconditionally instead of checking a per-tool "requires_confirmation"
flag. That flag, its FrontendToolSafety type, and everywhere it flowed
(ag-ui-bridge tool schema/state, ai-core gating, app-shell context, the
run-input builder, and all frontend tool definitions) are deleted.

Deletes the now-dead confirm UI (banner branch, tool-call cards, voice
dialog variant) along with useEngentyHumanInTheLoop and its registry,
which had no consumers left. The onFrontendToolApprove/Reject prop chain
is renamed onSandboxCommand* since sandbox-command confirmation is the
only thing left using it; decision/feedback artifacts and backend tool
approval are unaffected. Backend suspend/resume transport is unchanged.

Retry scheduler service-scope resolution to survive the dev boot race

startScheduler() resolved the service principal's scope exactly once at
boot. When the AI app boots ahead of core in the turbo dev stack, the
core HTTP call fails (network_error, status 0), the scope resolves to

resolution (core unreachable / JWT rejected — transient), and
startScheduler() retries the transient case on a bounded backoff
mirroring the existing reconcile deferral before giving up. The
resolution result is returned as a discriminated union so the two cases
log distinctly.

Add --db-restart to plugins install for schema exposure

Applying a module's migrations creates its tables, but the running API
only serves schemas listed in config.toml db-schemas, read at boot — so a
newly installed module's schema stays unreachable until the stack restarts.

Add an opt-in --db-restart flag (pair with --db-migrate) and an engenty
db restart subcommand that stop/starts the local stack so PostgREST
reloads the exposed schemas. Gated on a reachable local database, matching
the existing --db-migrate opt-in.
